title: Why God Feels Silent Tonight
hook: Feeling like God is quiet? Here are 4 biblical reasons — and 4 things you can do tonight.
script: Feeling like God is quiet? Here are 4 biblical reasons — and 4 things you can do tonight. One, refinement. Like James 1, testing grows endurance. Tonight, worship before answers: read Psalm 13 out loud. Two, preparation. Joseph heard nothing in prison, yet God was shaping him. Obey the small thing in front of you. Three, timing. Habakkuk 2:3 says the vision awaits an appointed time. Sit five minutes in quiet and breathe the name of Jesus. Four, sin or unresolved hurt can muffle your heart (Isaiah 59:2). Confess and forgive; 1 John 1:9 says He cleanses. Prayer: Lord, I choose worship, obedience, waiting, and repentance. Speak; your servant is listening.

title: If God Is Quiet: Do This Now
hook: If God feels silent right now, watch this.
script: If God feels silent right now, watch this. Silence in Scripture often means shaping, not absence. Israel waited generations, yet the Savior came right on time. Tonight, thank God for the quiet that sands your faith smooth. Like Samuel, say, “Speak, Lord,” then obey the last thing He told you. Like David, strengthen yourself in the Lord—sing a psalm before sleep. If your conscience stings, clear it: confess to God and plan one reconciliation (1 John 1:9; Matthew 5:24). Promise to hold: those who wait on the Lord renew their strength (Isaiah 40:31). Save this and replay whenever doubt returns.

title: Hear God In The Quiet
hook: This truth can change how you see the silence.
script: This truth can change how you see the silence. God’s quiet can mean He’s refining you, preparing the path, protecting His timing, or inviting repentance. Tonight, practice four moves. Worship before answers—declare three things God already is. Wait on purpose—sit two minutes in stillness after prayer. Obey the last clear nudge—send the text, apply, serve. Confess what’s blocking peace—name it, receive grace from 1 John 1:9, forgive as you were forgiven. Remember Elijah: the whisper came after the wind. Pray with me: Jesus, make me steady in the quiet. Your timing, not mine. Your voice above my overthinking. I’m listening. Amen.
